```{r Load Packages and Data, include = FALSE}

# Load packages
library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(here)
library(beepr)
library(peRReo)
library(kableExtra)
library(palmerpenguins)

library(mapdata)
library(mapproj)
library(sf)

library(scales)

# Load Meteorite Date
meteorites <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2019/2019-06-11/meteorites.csv")

```

### Introduction

- Meteorites provide physical evidence of material arriving on Earth from *space*

![](../Data/hothmeteorites.png)

- This analysis maps:
  - Geographic location
  - Classification as `Fell` or `Found`
  - Mass

### Data Preparation

- Meteorite data come from the Meteoritical Society through NASA, distributed by TidyTuesday project

```{r Prepare Data}
# Clean Dataset
meteorites_clean <- meteorites |>
  drop_na(lat, long, mass, fall, year)|>
  filter(
    between(lat, -90, 90),
    between(long, -180, 180),
    mass > 0,
    year >= 1900,
    !(lat == 0 & long == 0)) |>
  mutate(
    fall = factor(
      fall,
      levels = c("Found", "Fell")))

# Obtain country polygon coordinates
world <- map_data("world")
```

### Global Meteorite Distribution

```{r Global Meteorite Distribution}
#| label: fig-meteorite-map
#| fig-cap: "Recorded meteorite locations since 1900"
#| fig-alt: "World map displaying meteorite locations as colored circles. Larger circles indicate greater meteorite mass"
#| out-width: "90%"

# Make Palette
meteorite_colors <- c(
  "Found" = "#277DA1",
  "Fell" = "#F94144")

# Create the Map
meteorite_map <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon( # Draw country polygons from world
    data = world,
    aes(
      x = long,
      y = lat,
      group = group),
    fill = "#E8E5DF",
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_point(
    data = meteorites_clean, # Add meteorite locations
    aes(
      x = long,
      y = lat,
      color = fall,
      size = mass),
    alpha = 0.55) +
  coord_quickmap( # Preserve geographic proportions
    xlim = c(-180, 180),
    ylim = c(-60, 85),
    expand = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = meteorite_colors) + # Apply palette and logarithmic mass scale
  scale_size_continuous(
    trans = "log10",
    range = c(0.05, 2),
    labels = label_number(
      scale_cut = cut_short_scale())) +
  labs(
    title = "Meteorites Recorded Across Earth since 1900",
    subtitle = "Observations from a Galaxy Not So Far Away",
    color = "Record type:",
    size = "Mass (g)",
    caption = paste(
      "Source: Meteoritical Society and NASA;",
      "data distributed by TidyTuesday")) +
  theme_starwars(starwars_font = TRUE) + # STAR WARS THEME LFG
theme(
  axis.title = element_blank(),
  axis.text = element_blank(),
  axis.ticks = element_blank(),
  panel.background = element_rect(
    fill = "grey29",
    color = NA,
  ),
  plot.title = element_text(
    size = 20,
    face = "bold",
    color = "#F1E81F"
  ),
  plot.subtitle = element_text(
    size = 12,
    color = "white"
  ),
  plot.caption = element_text(
    size = 8,
    color = "grey75"
  ),
  legend.position = "bottom",
  legend.title = element_text(
    face = "bold",
    color = "#F1E81F"
  ),
  legend.text = element_text(color = "white")
)

meteorite_map
```

- @fig-meteorite-map shows the geographic distribution of recorded meteorites
  - Larger circles represent heavier meteorites.
  - Point size use a logarithmic scale because meteorite masses vary by several orders of magnitude.

### Interpretation

1.  Recordings are found across the globe
2.  `Found` greatly outnumber observed `Fell` meteors
3.  Concentrated in particular regions, could be artifact of sampling (and reduced ocean access)
